verdict.rationale: Several independent hands-on reports show the core Sentry product can be self-hosted: long-running instances, an install via git clone and ./install.sh, and Helm-chart deployments that 'just work'. However, the pack has no first-party self-hosting documentation, and users report real limits: releases lag the SaaS version, it needs a 16GB+ machine, setup can be prohibitively complex, and some upgrades break. missing for 10: first-party self-hosting documentation, evidence of feature parity with SaaS, lighter-weight deployment for small teams, reliably smooth upgrades.

support.subject: As an AI-native user, I can self-host the core product

citations.quote: A user has run self-hosted Sentry at work for a couple of years and says it has worked fantastically and is rock-solid once running.
installation is git clone, editing one or two config files, and running ./install.sh
A user deployed self-hosted Sentry with a Helm chart and says it 'just works'.
